sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Why was Rasachikitsa considered a unique system of medicine? Give two reasons in short phrases.
questions.answer: It dealt principally with mineral medicines; it used mercurial and non-mercurial preparations.

questions.q: Match two items of Column A with Column B (the rest are distracters): Ganit Kaumudi – Narayan Pandit; Mrig-pakshi-shastra – Hamsadeva; Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri – Faizi; Lilavati Vyakhya – Charak. Give the two correct pairs.
questions.answer: Ganit Kaumudi – Narayan Pandit; Mrigapakshishastra – Hamsadeva.
questions.note: April 2025 asked this with Faizi, Hamsadeva, Narayan Pandit and Charak as the options.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Name two treatises on Ayurveda written in the medieval period. (b) What does the Sarangadhara Samhita include?
questions.answer: (a) Sarangadhara Samhita and Bhavaprakasha (Chikitsasangraha). (b) Use of opium in materia medica and urine examination for diagnosis.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Akbar ordered mathematics to be made a subject of study. (b) Medieval Ayurveda progressed vigorously with royal patronage.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it lacked royal patronage.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Faizi, at Akbar's behest, translated ______ Bijaganita. Mahendra Suri developed the instrument ______.
questions.answer: Bhaskara's; Yantraraja.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) What were the two functions of karkhanas? (b) Name two subjects in the primary curriculum.
questions.answer: (a) Manufacturing and technical–vocational training. (b) Arithmetic and mensuration (also geometry, agriculture).

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Potato and chillies were introduced in the 16th–17th centuries. (b) Mango grafting was introduced by the Chinese.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – by the Jesuits of Goa.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Name two paper-making centres. (b) What was used for irrigation in Agra?
questions.answer: (a) Kashmir and Sialkot (Patna, Ahmedabad). (b) The Persian wheel.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Hamsadeva wrote ______ in the 13th century. Jahangir's court artists drew about ______ plants.
questions.answer: Mrigapakshishastra; 57.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) The Sukraniti describes preparation of gunpowder. (b) The Unani system was developed in India during the Mauryan period.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it came with Muslims about the 11th century.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) What is Firdausu-Hikmat? (b) Which book brought together Arabic, Persian and Ayurvedic medicine?
questions.answer: (a) A book by Ali-bin-Rabban summarising Greek and Indian medicine. (b) Majiny-e-Diyae.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Sawai Jai Singh II built ______ observatories. The Parameshvara and Mahabhaskariya families of ______ were astronomers.
questions.answer: five; Kerala.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Madrasas followed a set curriculum. (b) Most scientific works of this period were commentaries on earlier works.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) True.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Which Mughal emperor wrote the Tuzuk? (b) Who painted animals for Jahangir?
questions.answer: (a) Jahangir. (b) Mansur.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Saffron was cultivated in Kashmir. (b) Black pepper came from Kashmir.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – from the Western Ghats.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Why was Rasachikitsa a unique system of medicine?
questions.answer: It was a system of mineral medicines – mercurial and non-mercurial preparations – and the Siddhas used it for life-prolonging compositions.

questions.q: What were the two main functions of karkhanas?
questions.answer: They were manufacturing agencies supplying the royal household and government departments, and centres of technical and vocational training for young artisans.

questions.q: Who were the Parameshvara and Mahabhaskariya families?
questions.answer: Famous families of astronomers and almanac-makers of Kerala.

questions.q: Name any two Persian medical works of the medieval period.
questions.answer: Tibb-i-Firozshahi, Tibbi Aurangzebi, Majiny-e-Diyae and Mualajat-i-Dara Shikohi.

questions.q: How was gunpowder prepared according to Sukraniti?
questions.answer: From saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal in different ratios for different types of guns.

questions.q: What changes did medieval rulers make in primary school education?
questions.answer: They added arithmetic, mensuration, geometry, astronomy, accountancy, public administration and agriculture; Akbar made mathematics compulsory.

questions.q: Name any two crops introduced during the medieval period.
questions.answer: Tobacco, chillies, potato, guava, custard apple, cashew, pineapple (any two).

questions.q: What was the contribution of Jahangir in the field of biology?
questions.answer: In the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri he described about 36 species of animals and his court artists such as Mansur drew animals and about 57 plants accurately.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Discuss the developments in the field of medicine in medieval India.
questions.answer: Ayurveda progressed slowly because of lack of patronage, but Sarangadhara Samhita (use of opium, urine examination), Chikitsasangraha, Yogaratnakara and Bhavaprakasha were compiled. Rasachikitsa and Siddha used mineral medicines. The Unani Tibb system came with Muslims and works like Firdausu-Hikmat, Majiny-e-Diyae, Tibb-i-Firozshahi and Mualajat-i-Dara Shikohi combined Greek, Arabic, Persian and Ayurvedic knowledge.

questions.q: Write about astronomy in medieval India.
questions.answer: Commentaries on established ideas appeared; Mahendra Suri of Firoz Shah's court developed the Yantraraja; the Parameshvara and Mahabhaskariya families of Kerala were famous; Nilakantha Somasutvan commented on the Aryabhatiya; Kamalakara studied Islamic astronomy; Sawai Jai Singh II built observatories at Delhi, Ujjain, Varanasi, Mathura and Jaipur.

questions.q: Describe agriculture in the medieval period.
questions.answer: The pattern was similar to early India, with wheat, rice, barley, millets, pulses, oilseeds, cotton, sugarcane and indigo; new crops (tobacco, chillies, potato, guava, cashew, pineapple) came in the 16th–17th centuries; mango grafting was introduced by the Jesuits; irrigation by wells, tanks, canals, rahat, charas and the Persian wheel; the State introduced land measurement and classification.

questions.q: Write about mathematics in medieval India.
questions.answer: Narayana Pandit wrote Ganitakaumudi, Gangadhara the Lilavati Vyakhya, Nilakantha Somasutvan the Tantrasangraha, Ganesa Daivajna the Buddhivilasini; Faizi translated Bhaskara's Bijaganita; rules of trigonometry were given; Akbar made mathematics a subject of study.

questions.q: Explain the use of chemistry in paper-making and gunpowder.
questions.answer: Paper-making spread across Kashmir, Sialkot, Patna, Ahmedabad, Mysore and other centres with similar methods; the Mughals used gunpowder in gunnery, and Sukraniti gives ratios of saltpetre, sulphur and charcoal; fireworks and perfumes (attar of roses) were also developed.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Describe the education system and developments of science in the medieval period.
questions.answer: The Arab pattern of education led to maktabs and madrasas under royal patronage with a set curriculum; scholars from Arabia, Persia and Central Asia were invited; primary courses included arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, accountancy and agriculture. Karkhanas trained artisans. Works were produced in mathematics (Narayana Pandit, Gangadhara), biology (Hamsadeva, Jahangir), chemistry (paper, gunpowder), astronomy (Mahendra Suri, Jai Singh), medicine (Ayurveda and Unani) and agriculture (new crops), mostly commentaries; texts were translated between Sanskrit and Persian/Arabic.

questions.q: Write an essay on science and scientists in the medieval period.
questions.answer: Science continued earlier traditions and took Islamic and European influences. Mathematicians: Narayana Pandit, Gangadhara, Nilakantha, Ganesa Daivajna, Faizi. Biology: Hamsadeva and Jahangir. Chemistry: paper, gunpowder (Sukraniti), perfumes. Astronomy: Mahendra Suri, Kerala families, Sawai Jai Singh II's five observatories. Medicine: Ayurveda, Rasa, Siddha and Unani. Agriculture: new crops, grafting and irrigation devices. Most works were commentaries.

questions.q: Explain how irrigation was done and how agriculture developed in the medieval period.
questions.answer: Wells, tanks, canals, the rahat (Persian wheel), charas and dhenkli were used for irrigation; the Persian wheel was used near Agra. The State introduced a system of land measurement and classification, and new crops like tobacco, chillies, potato, guava, cashew and pineapple came in the 16th–17th centuries; opium was produced in Malwa and Bihar; Jesuits introduced mango grafting; Mughal gardens grew fruit trees.
